bullets.text: Full-year CR 95.3, meeting the 4-cent aggregate underwriting profit goal; Q1 CR 89.3, Q2 96.5, June 100.5; CL CR 88.9; Property disappointed by weather-related catastrophe underwriting losses.

Took larger rate increases to get ahead of step-function severity trends; deployed auto model 8.7 in 22 states (over half of premium); completed 24 auto model upgrades; deployed Property 4.0/4.1 to 16 states.
Personal Lines NPW crossed $36B milestone to $36.2B (+nearly $3B); Commercial Lines reached $8.0B NPW (+51% YOY), marking seven straight years of profitable double-digit premium growth.
Severity outpaced sophisticated models, especially in H2, and changed in a step function; driving returned to near pre-pandemic levels; ended 2021 with 0% prior accident year reserve development.
Personal Lines expense ratio 19.0 (vs. 19.9 in 2019); PL NAER -0.7 pts vs. 2019; CL expense ratio 19.6, with NAER -0.9 pts vs. 2019; LAE ratio +0.3 pts vs. 2020.

Investment portfolio topped $50B with 2.6% return (fixed-income slightly negative, equity index +27%); paid $1.50/share variable dividend plus $0.40/share quarterly; paid off $500M 3.75% Senior Notes; repurchased shares opportunistically.
Personal Lines added over 1.3M policies to end at 22.7M PIF; bundled Robinson customers grew nearly 13%; 21% of customers are Robinsons or hold multiple Progressive products.
Acquired Protective Insurance Corporation; expanded BOP to 17 states (now 34 states, >60% of CMP market); BQX logged 90+ carrier/product/state expansions; online buy on HQX reached 48 states.
Adjusted media spend to align with profitability goals amid rising loss costs; Dr. Rick ranked on Ad Age's most popular insurance ad characters list; Dr. Rick hardbound book sold out.

Annual theme of flexibility honored by sharing a nearly 560-piece mosaic with 560 employees; Gallup engagement placed Progressive in 97th percentile; people-of-color senior leadership rose from 10% to 16%.
